title: Don't Miss Your ITR Deadline if Your Accounts Need an Audit!
description: The deadline to file your Income Tax Return (ITR) for Financial Year 2025-26 (Assessment Year 2026-27) is **September 30, 2026**, if your accounts need to be .

faq.q: Who exactly needs to get their accounts audited for ITR purposes?
faq.a: Generally, businesses with turnover exceeding ₹1 crore (or ₹10 crore for 95% digital transactions) and professionals with gross receipts exceeding ₹50 lakhs in Financial Year 2025-26 need a tax audit. There are also specific rules for those opting out of presumptive taxation.

faq.q: What happens if I miss the September 30th deadline for audited accounts?
faq.a: If you miss the deadline, you will likely have to pay a late filing fee of up to ₹5,000. You may also lose the ability to carry forward certain losses to future years, and any tax refunds might be delayed.

faq.q: Can I revise my ITR after filing if I discover a mistake?
faq.a: Yes, if you file your original ITR by the September 30th deadline, you can generally revise it if you find any errors or omissions, typically until December 31, 2026.

faq.q: What documents do I need for an audited ITR?
faq.a: You'll need your financial statements (Profit & Loss Account, Balance Sheet), bank statements, invoices, bills, details of assets and liabilities, Form 26AS, AIS/TIS, and any other relevant financial records for the CA to conduct the audit.

faq.q: What is the difference between ITR-3 and ITR-4 forms?
faq.a: ITR-3 is for individuals and Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs) who have income from business or profession and do not opt for the presumptive taxation scheme. ITR-4 (Sugam) is for individuals, HUFs, and partnership firms whose total income includes business income under the presumptive taxation scheme (Sections 44AD, 44ADA, 44AE) and is below a certain limit.
